Mental Health in the Community

Community mental health — programmes, DMHP, family burden, rehabilitation, stigma reduction and emergency care.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe community mental health programmes
  • Explain family burden and support
  • Describe psychosocial rehabilitation
  • Reduce stigma and provide crisis care

In simple words

Most people with mental illness live and recover with their families. Community mental health delivers care where they live and keeps them out of institutions.

The National Mental Health Programme and DMHP

  • NMHP 1982 and revised DMHP from 1996
  • DMHP services: outpatient clinics, inpatient care, outreach, and records
  • Manpower: psychiatrist, clinical psychologist, psychiatric social worker and community nurse
  • Mobile mental health teams reach villages
  • Day-care and halfway homes support the transition back home

Family burden

  • Chronic care is often carried out by women at home
  • Burden rises with disability, aggression and limited coping
  • Assess burden at each visit; provide teaching, respite and counselling
  • Watch for abuse of the patient or neglect by the family

Stigma reduction

  • Negative labels stop treatment and damage recovery
  • Education, contact with recovered people and inclusion reduce stigma
  • Awareness camps, school programmes and community dialogues are used
  • The nurse uses respectful language in every interaction

🔴 Keep the person in the community

Community care maintains dignity, family life and work better than long institutional care. Rehabilitation means restoring the person’s role, not only reducing symptoms.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Mental Health in the Community keeps people in the community and prevents relapse.
  2. DMHP provides outreach, outpatient care and referral.
  3. Family burden assessment is part of every visit.
  4. Stigma reduction through education and inclusion.
  5. Family care givers need teaching, support and respite.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Day-care centres and halfway homes are part of care.
  2. Follow-up reduces default and relapse.
  3. Confidentiality is essential in small communities.
  4. Crisis management protects the patient and the family.
  5. Community nurses lead mental health awareness activities.

📌 Memory trick

Community mental health = P-I-R-S — Prevention, Identify, Rehabilitate, Support.

60-second revision

  • NMHP and DMHP take mental health care to districts.
  • Outreach visits find and support patients at home.
  • Family burden is assessed and supported.
  • Rehabilitation: skills, work, family integration.
  • Stigma reduced by education, contact and inclusion.

Test yourself

A community nurse supports a family of a mentally ill member by:

Answer: B. Family support includes teaching nursing care, counselling and arranging respite to sustain care at home.

DMHP provides:

Answer: B. The District Mental Health Programme provides outpatient care, outreach and follow-up services.

Assessment of family burden is done to:

Answer: B. Burden assessment identifies support needs and prevents exhaustion and abandonment of care.

Stigma is reduced mainly by:

Answer: B. Education and normalising contact with people who have recovered reduce fear and prejudice.

A halfway home provides:

Answer: B. A halfway home supports the person in moving from hospital back to independent family life.
